strings.name: Mary Kom
strings.summary: Kom rose from rural Manipur to win six women's world amateur boxing titles and a bronze at London 2012, the first Olympics with women's boxing. She returned to championship form after motherhood and served in India's Rajya Sabha. Injuries and age limits changed her competitive options; in 2026 she discussed opportunities to return through professional boxing.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Multiple world boxing titles and an Olympic medal expanded the international influence of Asian women's boxing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Raised in Manipur; sources differ between birth years 1982 and 1983 and also give different dates.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Six world titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won six women's world championship gold medals between 2002 and 2018.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained in boxing in Imphal after participating in athletics and other sports.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Olympic breakthrough
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won the women's 51 kg bronze medal in 2012.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses professional opportunities
strings.timeline.t1.text: At a Navi Mumbai event she expressed a desire to compete again; this was not a comeback result.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Tokyo round of sixteen
strings.timeline.t2.text: Lost to Colombia's Ingrit Valencia in the 51 kg division.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Sixth world championship
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won the 48 kg title in New Delhi, setting a women's record.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Enters the Rajya Sabha
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began a nominated parliamentary term that ended in 2022.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Asian Games gold
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the women's 51 kg title in Incheon.
strings.timeline.t6.title: London Olympic bronze
strings.timeline.t6.text: Reached the podium at the first Olympics to include women's boxing.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First world title
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won the 45 kg gold in Antalya, beginning her championship sequence.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Domestic breakthrough
strings.timeline.t8.text: After training in Imphal, won the Manipur championship and advanced toward elite competition.
